Canonical PDF includes listed 2026 amendments; no complete VAT survey claimed.

conclusion: The opaque numbers can now be explained: Article 10 ordinary registration, Article 11 conditional domestic small-enterprise exemption without credit, Article 12 specified cross-border duties including additional registration for Article 11 purchasers. Article 20(2)(b) shifts covered Malta-taxable general business-service liability from a non-established/non-Article-10 supplier to the recipient. Actual transaction classification remains fact-dependent rather than an unresolved legal definition.

proposedPublicPatch.learningSummary: Your domestic small-business VAT exemption does not necessarily cover VAT you must account for on foreign software. An Article 11 business can also need Article 12 registration for a covered foreign-service purchase, by the date it receives the service.

sections.heading: Know what your registration does
paragraphs: Article 10 is the ordinary VAT registration discussed here: VAT applies to taxable supplies taking place in Malta, while recovery of purchase VAT depends on the applicable credit rules. Article 11 is the domestic small-enterprise scheme for eligible Malta-established businesses; its exemption is without input-tax credit. Eligibility and turnover calculation are governed by the Sixth Schedule.

Article 12 deals with specified cross-border transactions. It can be required alongside Article 11: the Act expressly says an Article 11 business receiving services for which it must pay VAT must also register under Article 12. The domestic sales exemption is therefore not an exemption from every foreign purchase.

sections.heading: Check who must account for VAT on the foreign service
paragraphs: For the general business-services case in Article 20(2)(b), a taxable service received in Malta from a supplier not established there and not Article 10-registered can make the Maltese recipient liable for the tax. Establish the actual service, place of supply and supplier status; the provision also addresses a Maltese fixed establishment that does not intervene in the supply.

If you are a Malta-established taxable person outside Article 10 registration and receive a service for which Article 20(2) makes you liable, Article 12(3) requires registration by the date you receive it. For an Article 11 support business buying covered foreign cloud access, that purchase duty is separate from how its American sale is treated. Article 12 itself does not provide input-tax recovery.

sections.heading: For the sale, establish who receives your service
paragraphs: The VAT Act’s Third Schedule item 2(a) generally follows the business customer or the fixed establishment receiving the service, subject to exceptions. MTCA’s American-buyer example accepts sufficient appropriate evidence that the customer purchases for its business even though it has no EU VAT number.

So the missing EU number does not automatically make your buyer a consumer. Establish its business purpose, the receiving establishment and the kind of service. An American address alone does not answer those questions. In the cloud example, those facts decide the sale analysis; your own status and purchase liability decide the separate registration question.

sections.heading: The other-EU service branch has its own trigger
paragraphs: Article 12(3a) separately concerns a Malta-established taxable person outside Article 10 supplying services in another EU Member State for which the recipient alone pays VAT under Article 196. Registration is due by the date of that supply. An American customer is not that other Member State.

proposedPublicPatch.practicalOutput: Identify your actual registration and the foreign service’s place of supply and supplier status before receiving it; complete any required Article 12 registration by that date.
limitations: This explains the specified registration and service-liability rules, not a complete eligibility, turnover, credit, rate, invoice or VAT-return decision. The MTCA service notes remain nonbinding, are not Article 75 instructions and have inconsistent printed dates; the current Act controls. Actual U.S. taxes remain separate.

proposedPublicPatch.learningSummary: An American buyer need not get a Polish login for the covered ordinary online handoff. The supplier first checks the actual issuer and transaction: Poland’s 2026 phase dates and temporary exceptions do not exempt every invoice to America.

sections.heading: Check the issuer and the 2026 transition
paragraphs: The Ministry’s scope page starts mandatory issuance on 1 February 2026 for taxpayers whose 2024 sales including VAT exceeded PLN 200 million, and on 1 April 2026 for the others subject to exclusions. Through 31 December 2026, the temporary outside-KSeF route covers the stated paper/electronic invoices where the relevant monthly gross sales do not exceed PLN 10,000; check the applicable counting rules.

An issuer with neither its business seat nor a fixed establishment in Poland is excluded. A foreign issuer with a Polish fixed establishment is also excluded where that establishment does not participate in the supply. Consumer invoices and specified transaction/procedure categories have other exclusions. An American customer is therefore not, by itself, an exemption for a covered Polish supplier.

sections.heading: Send the customer a readable version of the issued invoice
paragraphs: For the covered ordinary online process, the Ministry FAQ addresses foreign customers outside the EU and without a Polish NIP tax identifier. Issue through KSeF, Poland’s National e-Invoice System, then provide the customer’s copy through an agreed channel. The buyer need not acquire a Polish login merely to pay you.

The customer version may be in English, but its substance must match the XML, the structured record sent to KSeF. Include the applicable QR code and KSeF reference. Agree how the buyer receives it and retain that delivery record; do not create a second, inconsistent invoice.

sections.heading: Keep delivery evidence separate from the invoice
paragraphs: If an American customer later disputes monthly support, the issued invoice and matching copy identify the bill. They do not establish which support was accepted. Keep acceptance protocols or shipment records separately; the FAQ says they are not simply attachments carried inside KSeF.

Reconcile payment, currency differences and corrections to the appropriate invoice records. Offline and outage modes have different QR and resubmission conditions, so do not copy this online sequence into those situations.

limitations: The described process is ordinary online issuance, not offline/outage contingencies. The 2026 transition route and exclusions require actual issuer, establishment, transaction and invoice-total facts; no universal VAT, withholding or U.S. tax outcome is supplied.

proposedPublicPatch.title: What proves a Latvian goods export, and what if an advance remains unfulfilled?
proposedPublicPatch.seoTitle: Latvian export VAT: customs proof and six-month advance rule
proposedPublicPatch.description: Use the stated export evidence and read the six-month advance consequence with its manufacturing/start qualifications.
proposedPublicPatch.learningSummary: For a Latvian goods export, the American invoice and payment are not the full proof. The current Cabinet rule identifies export documents; the VAT Law also denies the zero rate for specified unfulfilled advances after six months, subject to express qualifications.

sections.heading: Obtain the export declaration and support the actual exit
paragraphs: Section 43(1) applies a zero rate to goods exports, but section 51 denies it without the required proof. Cabinet Regulation 17 paragraph 15 identifies the export customs declaration drawn up under customs rules as an export-evidencing document.

To establish that goods actually left, paragraph 16 permits Customs to receive a combination of at least two of the following documents: international freight documents or copies, contracts with recipients in third countries or territories, and documents proving payment for the export. This does not mean that any two papers automatically grant the VAT rate.

Paragraph 17 normally places the documents in the exporting registered taxpayer’s name. They may also be in the forwarder’s, exporter’s or representative’s name where the export fact can be proved. Paragraph 19 permits other unequivocal documents alongside the stated records. Connect those documents to the actual goods and movement, rather than rely on the American invoice address.

sections.heading: If dispatch has not started after six months, check the tax consequence
paragraphs: For the covered advance-request VAT invoice, section 51(4) denies the zero rate if goods have not been dispatched or services have not started within six months from receipt of the advance. Section 51(5) excludes specified contract-based goods whose technological manufacturing process exceeds six months, and supplies/services already started when the advance was received.

Section 124(2) places tax calculated under that advance rule in the tax period following the six-month period counted from advance receipt. Establish the actual dates and whether a qualification applies; the goods-export answer does not automatically apply to ordinary training or support fees.

sections.heading: Use the Latvian text rather than the outdated English version
paragraphs: The English translation ends its validity in 2024 and omits later amendments. The current Latvian statute and the named Cabinet provisions were read with AI-assisted English interpretation for this explanation.

proposedPublicPatch.practicalOutput: Obtain the applicable export proof and check actual advance/dispatch dates and qualifications before making the VAT entry.
limitations: This concerns ordinary commercial export evidence and the specified advance rule, not every zero-rated service, special shipment or U.S. import. Actual customs acceptance, tax amount and period facts still need confirmation.

sections.heading: Establish the applicant and described filing route
paragraphs: WIPO’s filing notes define the office of origin as the office where your basic mark is applied for or registered and through which the international application is submitted. You also need entitlement through the relevant nationality, domicile or real and effective industrial/commercial establishment connection. The office of origin may require proof under its domestic law and practice. Cyprus’s preparation page lists a Cypriot natural-person national, a legal person established there or a person with an actual active industrial/commercial establishment there. Cyprus describes English MM2 through its Intellectual Property Section, with MM18 for a U.S. designation. Confirm the current submission procedure, basic-mark details and actual applicant. National examination still follows; the international filing is not a granted American right.

sections.heading: Review the statements before signing
paragraphs: The March 2026 WIPO MM18 form includes genuine intent to use, authority to execute for the applicant, and statements based on reasonable inquiry with evidentiary support. It requires the prescribed English declaration without alterations and the mandatory signature/execution details.

If the Cyprus parent owns the basic mark but an American subsidiary will operate, establish the actual applicant and authorised signer, and the facts supporting the statements. The subsidiary’s incorporation does not supply the parent’s declaration facts. Check the sign, goods/services, current fees and examination responsibilities; describe a pending filing accurately in commercial discussions.

sections.heading: Start with whose account it will be
paragraphs: Article 13 concerns resident accounts at non-resident banks. Identify the holder, bank legal entity and account type. The Moldovan parent’s own foreign account is a different fact from an account of a separately incorporated American subsidiary, whose residence and rules need separate analysis.
The general branch requires NBM authorisation subject to listed exceptions. Convenience or a customer’s preference for an American account is not itself an exception.

sections.heading: Check the exact purpose and onward payment
paragraphs: The export-collection branch added in 2025 concerns goods and/or services proceeds exclusively for export with final crediting to licensed banks in Moldova. Establish those receipts and the onward flow; do not infer general treasury permission.

Regulation 216, incorporating Decision 255/2025 effective 1 January 2026, also addresses accounts opened without NBM authorisation. Paragraph 12 requires receipts, retention and use to follow the purpose for which the account was opened. When the purpose is achieved, it requires closure and return of balances under the regulation, with stated exceptions.

Paragraph 65 has a general closing-balance exception for a payment/transfer that either needs no currency authorisation or has the required authorisation. That does not itself establish that any proposed American expense satisfies the particular export-only collection purpose and statutory final-crediting condition.

The monthly account report in Chapter VII is expressly for accounts opened under NBM authorisation. Do not copy its reporting route automatically onto an exempt account or infer that no separate tax or other reporting duty exists.

proposedPublicPatch.title: Which Bulgarian controlled-export documents apply to your supply?
proposedPublicPatch.seoTitle: Bulgarian controlled exports: classification, translations and application documents
proposedPublicPatch.description: Classify the actual supply first, then use the relevant application route and the published 2026 documentary changes.
proposedPublicPatch.learningSummary: An order for equipment or know-how does not establish export permission. The July 2026 implementing amendment resolves the old EU-reference issue and changes parts of the application packet, but the correct documents still depend on the actual supply and authorisation route.

sections.heading: Identify what is supplied before choosing the application
paragraphs: The 2024 compilation describes export, transfer, transit and technical-assistance regimes under Regulation 2021/821. Establish the actual item, software, technology or assistance, destination, participants, end user and intended use. Not every manual is controlled, but a “brand licence” label does not clear a technical supply.

Check whether a general authorisation or another route applies before assuming an individual or global national application is appropriate. A paid order is not authorisation: establish any required permission and its conditions before making the covered supply.

sections.heading: Match the documents to the actual authorisation route
paragraphs: The register describes applications by persons with the relevant registration. Its document list includes application and authorisation forms, end-user/end-use or import-certificate evidence, the contract or order, transaction participants and their activity rights, and manufacturer technical information with origin/acquisition evidence. Treat that list as a starting point, not a complete current application.

The July 2026 amendment changes the technical-document requirements and adds route-specific internal-compliance and large-project requirements. The large-project route has its own packet, including project description and participant evidence; specified substitute declarations are permitted where the relevant country’s law does not issue the named official document. Confirm the route before deciding which evidence is needed.

Required foreign-language documents must have a certified Bulgarian translation. The amendment defines certification by the translator’s name and signature; it does not add a universal notarisation requirement. It also removes the separate paid-fee-document requirement when payment is electronic. That is an evidence exception, not a fee waiver.

sections.heading: The older EU reference is reconciled; the fee amount is not
paragraphs: Regulation 2021/821 Article 31 repeals Regulation 428/2009 and directs old references to the new regulation using the correlation table. It preserves the relevant older provisions for export-authorisation applications made before 9 September 2021. The final July 2026 Bulgarian decree also replaces 428/2009 references throughout the implementing text with 2021/821.

The June 2026 statutory amendment renamed the responsible ministry, and the July decree follows that name change. The live register still links forms under the ministerial order of 21 May 2026, including 38/39 and 40/41. Use the current form for the applicable route rather than treating the older register wording as an alternative legal framework.
No fee amount is verified from the mixed descriptions. These specific amendments were read; they do not amount to a complete survey of later national law or the current control list.

proposedPublicPatch.title: When could the signed U.S.–Vietnam tax agreement affect a payment?
proposedPublicPatch.seoTitle: U.S.–Vietnam tax agreement: entry conditions and withholding timing
proposedPublicPatch.description: The agreement specifies entry and payment-effect conditions, but the current operative status remains unconfirmed here.
proposedPublicPatch.learningSummary: The signed agreement does not make a reduced withholding rate available by itself. Article 29 separates entry into force from the date its withholding provisions would apply; this review has not established that those conditions have occurred.

sections.heading: First establish entry into force, then the payment date
paragraphs: The Treasury agreement dated 7 July 2015 requires ratification or approval under both countries’ applicable procedures and written diplomatic notifications when those procedures are complete. Article 29 says the agreement enters into force on the date of the later notification. Finding the signed document does not establish that this happened.

For withholding, the agreement would apply to amounts paid or credited on or after 1 January of the year immediately following the year of entry into force. For other taxes, the stated start is Vietnamese taxable years and U.S. taxable periods beginning on or after that following 1 January. Article 27 information-exchange and administrative-assistance provisions instead take effect from entry into force, regardless of the taxable year or period concerned. Do not use the signature date as a universal start date.

sections.heading: The dated status evidence does not settle today’s treatment
paragraphs: A Vietnamese Ministry of Finance draft report dated 17 July 2025 expressly described the U.S. agreement among those not yet effective. That is positive evidence of the draft’s stated position at that date, not proof that no later change occurred. Vietnam is also absent from the reviewed IRS income-tax treaty index, but list absence alone is not a definitive current status determination.

Current operative status remains unconfirmed here. Withholding is tax deducted before you receive a payment. Keep the full fee, possible deduction and expected receipt separate until current authority and the actual payment and recipient establish the treatment. Neither the signed agreement nor this dated report supplies an automatic royalty rate.

sections.heading: Keep the equipment question separate from the tax assumption
paragraphs: In the fictional maintenance example, the American operator also needs a specialised Vietnamese test device with no identified American replacement or service provider. Even an established payment treatment would not make that device deliverable or serviceable.

Vietnam Customs’ commercial-export guide addresses prohibited products, specialised inspection or licensing, declarations and temporary-export situations. Identify whether the actual item is sold, moved temporarily or replaced locally before costing the shipment. No equipment category is verified here; the U.S. importer’s duties and ongoing serviceability also need assessment. Software rights and remote support are not decided by the goods procedure.
